review_scope: Initial source and retained local-log review was read-only. Later coordinator-authorized native Linux related gates are separately bound below; no product edits or router access by reviewer.
implementation: One private lazy Vec on DnsDaemon is taken by the normal UDP prepared-answer path, used by internal owned-Name parsing, and reclaimed after synchronous answer/forward submission. Existing walk_name validation is reused unchanged.
lifetime_and_error_review: Header errors occur before taking the stored buffer. Question-count/decode errors return the same scratch, including partial labels; the next decode clears its length before appending.
Only successful walk_name creates an owned Name. The original cursor and extra=4 footer bounds remain unchanged, so rrtype/class reads retain their previous safety contract.
The closure contains all local/cache/stale/policy/upstream Result returns. Both success and error results reach the final Name-to-buffer reclamation.
QueryResult contains owned reply Vecs or an ID, never a borrowed Name. Retained cache replies cannot be overwritten by later scratch reuse.

Forwarding still reparses the packet in the existing transaction table and stores independent owned upstream Question, recipient Name, packet and key. No pending forwarding object aliases this scratch.
The change is confined to answer_udp_prepared_with_local; other parsing APIs, stale refresh and asynchronous forwarding ownership remain unchanged.

resource_review.bound_basis: walk_name rejects an overlong label before appending it. Only this private scratch path owns the retained Vec; the pinned Rust1.98.1 amortized growth is max(2*capacity, required), so retention is bounded. No per-name pool, shrinking or extra reserve policy was introduced.
resource_review.tradeoff: A lazily allocated name buffer and its amortized spare capacity remain until daemon destruction; this is retained bounded state, not a zero-memory change.

resolved_review_points: The original pointer-loop fixture failed before producing partial scratch. Added truncation and invalid-label cases now verify partial bytes and unchanged pointer before subsequent valid reuse.
Added NameTooLong recovery and a valid follow-up query. The new overlong fixture is257 wire bytes; the existing wire tests separately retain the exact256-byte boundary.
The original general capacity256 claim was false for irregular labels. The final comment and fresh-daemon irregular fixture correctly retain the380-byte example without changing allocation policy.

local_evidence.scope: Existing author logs were inspected, not independently rerun locally. Final changes after f0a96480 are fixture coverage and a capacity comment; the completed native Linux related gates are separately bound below.

limitations: Successful source review and local checks are not full candidate compatibility/44-family qualification or SDK performance acceptance.
No allocation-count, CPU, throughput or latency improvement is measured by this review. The independent F-based prototype is not combined with stage diagnostics or other prototypes.
